prompt:
A small ball bearing of mass 0.0500 kg is released from rest into a tall glass cylinder filled with viscous liquid. The acceleration of free fall is 9.81 m s^-2.
(a) State the acceleration of the ball bearing at the exact instant of release before drag acts. [1]
(b) At a later instant, the upward viscous drag force on the ball bearing is 0.320 N. Calculate the downward acceleration of the ball bearing at this instant. [2]
(c) The ball bearing reaches terminal velocity before it hits the bottom of the cylinder. State the magnitude of the drag force acting on it at terminal velocity. [1]
hints: At release, drag is zero, so what is the acceleration?
Find weight W = mg first, then subtract drag to find net force.
solution:
(a) Acceleration at release = 9.81 m s^-2.
(b) Weight W = mg = 0.0500 kg x 9.81 m s^-2 = 0.4905 N.
Net force F_net = W - D = 0.4905 N - 0.320 N = 0.1705 N.
Acceleration a = F_net / m = 0.1705 N / 0.0500 kg = 3.41 m s^-2.
(c) At terminal velocity, D = W = 0.491 N.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: (a) At t = 0, D = 0 so a = g = 9.81 m s^-2.
Step 5: (c) At terminal velocity, D = W = 0.491 N.
